```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(p8105.datasets)
library(plotly)
library(flexdashboard)
library(longpca)
library(rvest)
source("source/mean_and_sd.R")
source("source/nsduh_process.R")

## Load and process data
data(rest_inspec)
```


```{r}
im = make_interaction_model(rest_inspec, 0 ~ score * violation_description, parse_text = TRUE, to_lower = TRUE)
core_im = core(im, core_threshold = 10)
diagnose(im)
pca = pca(core_im, k = 6)
pcs = rotate(pca)

streaks(pcs)

pcs$column_features |> 
  arrange(vpc_1_columns)

pcs$row_features |> 
  arrange(desc(vpc_3_rows))


ggplot(rest_inspec, aes(x = score)) +
  geom_histogram()
```

## Prove that lists can have anything:
```{r}
l = list(
  vec_numeric = 5:17,
  mat = matrix(1:8, nrow = 2, ncol = 4, byrow = T)
)
```

## `for` loops next:
```{r}
list_norm = list(
  a = rnorm(20, 3, 4),
  b = rnorm(20, -14, 3),
  c = rnorm(20, 1000, 10000),
  d = rnorm(20, 0, 1)
  )
```

## Get mean and SD for each sample:
```{r}
mean_and_sd(list_norm[[1]])
mean_and_sd(list_norm[[2]])
mean_and_sd(list_norm[[3]])
mean_and_sd(list_norm[[4]])
```


## Do it with iteration:
```{r}
output = vector("list", length = 4)

for (i in 1:4) {
  output[[i]] = mean_and_sd(list_norm[[i]])
}

print(output)
```

## But... this is wayyy better!
```{r}
output = map(list_norm, mean_and_sd)
print(output)

output = map_df(list_norm, median)
print(output)

output = map(list_norm, IQR)
print(output)

output = map_dbl(list_norm, median)
print(output)
```

```{r}
listcol_df = 
  tibble(
    name = c("a", "b", "c", "d"),
    samp = list_norm
  )

listcol_df |> pull(name)

listcol_df |> pull(samp)
```

## Iterate the list:
```{r}
## Run map on a column of a data frame:
map(pull(listcol_df, samp), mean_and_sd) 
```
## Really cool stuff
```{r}
### Create a new column with a mapped result:
listcol_df |> 
  mutate(
    output = map(samp, mean_and_sd)
  )

square = function(x){
  x_squ = x^2
  x_squ
}

### Do it with a df
meta = listcol_df |> 
  mutate(
    output = map_df(samp, mean_and_sd)
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    output = output |> 
      mutate(var = 
               map(s, square))
  )

### Do it with a dbl
listcol_df |> 
  mutate(
    output = map_dbl(samp, median)
  )
```

## Work with NSDUH:
```{r}
nsduh_table <- function(html, table_num) {
  
  table = 
    html |> 
    html_table() |> 
    nth(table_num) |>
    slice(-1) |> 
    select(-contains("P Value")) |>
    pivot_longer(
      -State,
      names_to = "age_year", 
      values_to = "percent") |>
    separate(age_year, into = c("age", "year"), sep = "\\(") |>
    mutate(
      year = str_replace(year, "\\)", ""),
      percent = str_replace(percent, "[a-c]$", ""),
      percent = as.numeric(percent)) |>
    filter(!(State %in% c("Total U.S.", "Northeast", "Midwest", "South", "West")))
  
  table
}




nsduh_url = "https://www.samhsa.gov/data/sites/default/files/NSDUHsaeShortTermCHG2015/NSDUHsaeShortTermCHG2015.htm"

nsduh_html = read_html(nsduh_url)

output = vector("list", 3)

for (i in c(1, 4, 5)) {
  output[[i]] = nsduh_table(nsduh_html, i)
}

nsduh_results = bind_rows(output)
```


## example process:
```{r}
output = map(table_nums, nsduh_process, html = nsduh_html)

nsduh_results = 
  map(c(1, 4, 5), nsduh_table, html = nsduh_html) |> 
  bind_rows()
```

```{r}
nsduh_df = 
  tibble(
    drug = c("marj", "cocaine", "heroin"),
    num = c(1, 4, 5)
  ) |> 
  mutate(table = map(num, nsduh_table, html = nsduh_html)) |> 
  select(-num) |> 
  unnest(table)


nsduh_df |> 
  filter(age == "12-17") |> 
  mutate(State = fct_reorder(State, percent)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = State, y = percent, color = year)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_grid(. ~ drug)
```

```{r}
data("weather_df")

weather_df = 
  weather_df |> 
  nest(data = date:tmin)
```

what if i want to do a regression of tmax on tmin for each situation:
```{r}
lm(tmax ~ tmin, data = pull(weather_df, data)[[1]])
lm(tmax ~ tmin, data = pull(weather_df, data)[[2]])
lm(tmax ~ tmin, data = pull(weather_df, data)[[3]])

## Create a function to do the same thing:
weather_lm = function(input_data) {
  lm(tmax ~ tmin, data = input_data)
}

weather_lm(pull(weather_df, data)[[1]])

lm_master = weather_df |> 
  mutate(
    lm_fits = map(data, weather_lm),
    lm_sum = map(lm_fits, summary)
  )
```
